questions.q: Which blood vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
questions.why: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; the pulmonary artery takes it to the lungs.

questions.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle?
options: It pumps blood at higher pressure around the whole body.
It pumps blood only to the lungs.
It receives blood from the vena cava.
It must hold a larger volume of blood.
questions.why: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta, all round the body, so it needs more pressure.

questions.q: What is the function of lymphocytes?
questions.why: Lymphocytes produce antibodies; phagocytes engulf pathogens by phagocytosis.

questions.q: State one advantage of a double circulation in a mammal.
questions.model: Blood is pumped again after the lungs, so it reaches the body at high pressure, giving faster delivery of oxygen and glucose to respiring tissues.
points: blood reaches the body at high pressure (pumped twice)
faster delivery of oxygen / glucose to tissues
accept: lower pressure to lungs protects capillaries, or oxygenated and deoxygenated blood kept separate
